capabilities.name: Memory
capabilities.summary: What Claude keeps between sessions, and what you can ask it to forget.

capabilities.name: Projects
capabilities.summary: A space that keeps files and instructions together so you stop repeating context in every chat.
capabilities.unlocks: Shared context and files for a body of work

capabilities.name: Artifacts
capabilities.summary: A working pane next to the chat for documents, code and visuals you can edit in place.
capabilities.unlocks: Inspectable, editable output alongside the chat

capabilities.name: File creation
capabilities.summary: Claude producing and editing real files, spreadsheets, slides and documents, not just pasted text.
capabilities.unlocks: Real files you can open in your own apps

capabilities.name: Custom visuals
capabilities.summary: Claude drawing a chart or diagram built for your data rather than describing one in words.
capabilities.unlocks: Charts and diagrams built for the answer

capabilities.name: Scheduled tasks
capabilities.summary: A saved prompt that runs on a clock, so the work happens without you opening anything.

capabilities.name: Computer use
capabilities.summary: Claude operating your computer directly, clicking and typing in apps that have no other way in.
capabilities.unlocks: Steps in apps that have no other integration

capabilities.name: Dispatch
capabilities.summary: Send Claude a job and walk away. It keeps working after you close the tab or the app.
capabilities.unlocks: Long jobs started from a phone and picked up later

capabilities.name: Web search
capabilities.summary: Claude searching the live web and citing what it used, instead of relying only on training data.

capabilities.name: Chat search
capabilities.summary: Search across your own past conversations instead of scrolling to find one.
capabilities.unlocks: Finding a thread from weeks ago

capabilities.name: Skills
capabilities.summary: Packaged know how Claude loads when it fits the job, such as building a deck or reading a PDF.

capabilities.name: Plugins
capabilities.summary: Bundles of commands, agents and hooks you install for your own stack and share with a team.

capabilities.name: Connectors
capabilities.summary: Read or write access to a tool you already use, each with its own scopes you switch on by hand.
capabilities.unlocks: Your own mail, files and tickets

capabilities.name: MCP local
capabilities.summary: A local server that a Model Context Protocol client can reach from inside Code.
capabilities.unlocks: Local tools reachable from a prompt

capabilities.name: Reflect
capabilities.summary: Claude checking its own draft answer against the question before it replies.
capabilities.unlocks: A second pass before the final answer

capabilities.name: Interactive apps
capabilities.summary: A small interactive tool rendered inside the chat, such as a form or a mini app, instead of plain text.
capabilities.unlocks: Small tools rendered in the chat itself

bullets: Layouts and spacing survive the move.

bullets: One folder, shared by the whole team.

bullets: No upload, it reads the open tab.

alternative.text: If you would rather stay inside your mail client, use Claude in Outlook and ask for the same summary by hand each morning. Slower, but nothing to connect.

followUps: Draft replies for the “needs a reply today” list, but do not send them.
Every Friday, tell me who I have kept waiting the longest.
pitfalls: It will not send replies unless you ask it to. Keep it read only until you trust the summary.
Very large mailboxes get truncated. Give it a window, not your whole archive.
usecases.planNote: Connectors and scheduled tasks sit on the paid personal plans as of 7 September 2026
usecases.promptTemplate: Every weekday at 08:00, read my unread mail from the last 24 hours. Group it into three lists: needs a reply today, waiting on someone else, and safe to archive. For each item give me the sender, one line of context, and a suggested next step. Keep the whole thing under {{length}} and flag anything from {{sender}} first.

setup.note: read scope is enough for this route
setup.text: Allow read access to mail only
Save the prompt as a task at 08:00

usecases.title: Tidy my inbox every morning
why: Cowork can hold a job that repeats, so you set it up once rather than asking each day.
Your mail already lives in Microsoft 365, and there is a connector for it.
Nothing here needs code, so you can undo it from the same screen you set it up in.

alternative.text: Ask Chat by hand each evening with your calendar pasted in. No setup, but you have to remember to ask.

followUps: Pull the last email thread with each external attendee.
Flag any meeting that clashes with another one.
pitfalls: It only knows what is on the connected calendar, so add guests manually if you invited them elsewhere.
Recurring meetings all look the same to it unless the title changes.
usecases.planNote: Scheduled tasks sit on the paid personal plans as of 7 September 2026

setup.note: Settings, Connectors, Google Calendar or Microsoft 365

setup.text: Save the prompt as a task at 07:30

usecases.title: Prepare me for tomorrow's meetings
why: A repeating job means you never have to remember to ask for it.
Calendar and mail already sit behind the same connector.
You can turn it off from the same task list you set it up in.

alternative.text: Paste your calendar and sent mail into Chat by hand on Friday and ask for the same report.

followUps: Turn this into three bullet points I can paste into Slack.
Compare this week to last week and flag anything that slipped.

pitfalls: It only sees what happened in connected tools, not conversations that happened in person.
Vague calendar titles produce a vague report. Rename recurring events once and it improves.
usecases.planNote: Scheduled tasks sit on the paid personal plans as of 7 September 2026

setup.note: pick a time before your week ends
setup.text: Save the prompt as a task on Fridays

Rename the files in one folder to a consistent pattern.

setup.text: Ask for the sections you actually use

why: Chat turns loose notes into a structured draft in one pass.

followUps: Write a regression test that would have caught this.
Explain the root cause in plain language for the ticket.

pitfalls: Give it a way to reproduce the bug. A guess without a repro step is a guess.
Review the diff before merging. It edits real files with your permission, not blind trust.

why: Code reads and edits your actual repository, not a pasted snippet.
It can run your tests to check the fix before you do.
You approve each file change, so nothing merges without you seeing it.

why: Code can check out the branch and run the tests, not just read a diff.

why: Code can run the real test suite after each change, not just describe one.

why: Dispatch is built for exactly this: send it, walk away, come back to a result.
The mobile app needs nothing more than a phone to get a real job started.
A nudge when the result lands means you do not have to keep checking.
